About.manifesto:
Mythen formen Menschen. Scrollen nicht. Das sind kurze, filmische Werke über die größten Geschichten der Welt. Nur ein paar Minuten. Richtig gemacht. Nicht, um dich an Glas zu ketten. Sondern um dich mit etwas Tragfähigem zurück in die Welt zu schicken.

Privacy.title: PRIVACY
Privacy.s1Body: Fjorr is built to be simple. Watching stays open. Accounts are optional membership — for a Scout name, watch history, and contributions when you choose to join. We don't sell your data or follow you around the internet for ads.
Privacy.s2p1: We collect personal information when you choose to give it: your email for the newsletter, and — if you create an account — your email for magic-link sign-in plus the Scout name and profile details you save.
Privacy.s2p2: Like most sites, our hosting provider receives basic server logs: browser, device, approximate location (city-level), pages visited, and when. These help keep Fjorr secure and running; they don't identify you as a person on their own.
Privacy.s2p3: If you watch while signed in, we may store watch progress and film logs on your account so your Voyages can remember what you've seen. Device-local progress may also be stored in your browser until you sign in.
Privacy.s3Body: Newsletter email is only for film updates and the occasional note — unsubscribe anytime. Account email is only for signing you in (magic link) and account-related messages. We don't share, sell, or trade your email.
Privacy.s4Item2: Run advertising trackers or ad IDs
Privacy.s4Item4: Require an account to watch films
Privacy.s4Item5: Share Scout profiles publicly unless you turn that on
Privacy.s4Item6: Use tracking cookies for third-party ads
Privacy.s5Body: We use Mux to stream films — it may collect anonymous playback data so video works. Supabase stores account and membership data when you sign in. If we use an email service for the newsletter or magic links, it stores your address only to reach you. We'll update this page if that changes.
Privacy.s6Body: Depending on where you live, you may have rights to access, correct, or delete personal data. Email us and we'll help — including deleting an account and associated membership data. Unsubscribe removes you from the newsletter list right away.
Privacy.s7Body: If what we collect or how Fjorr works ever changes, we'll update this page.
Privacy.s8Body: If you have questions, you can reach us at:

Terms.s1Body: Fjorr ist ein Ort für Kurzfilme und Geschichten. Wenn du hier bist und zuschaust, gelten diese Regeln.
Terms.s2Body: Schau dir unsere Filme an und teile sie, so viel du möchtest — für den persönlichen Gebrauch. Kopiere oder remixe sie nur nicht ohne Erlaubnis. Und nutze die Website nicht auf eine Weise, die es allen anderen schwerer macht.
Terms.s3Body: Alle Filme, Bilder, Texte und Logos auf Fjorr gehören uns oder den Personen, die sie erstellt haben. Für eine kommerzielle Nutzung benötigst du unsere Erlaubnis.
Terms.s4Body: Fjorr wird „wie besehen“ angeboten. Wir können keine Perfektion oder ununterbrochenen Zugriff garantieren, bemühen uns aber stets, alles reibungslos am Laufen zu halten.
Terms.s5Body: Soweit gesetzlich zulässig, haftet Fjorr nicht für Schäden im Zusammenhang mit der Nutzung der Website.
Terms.s6Body: Diese Bedingungen können sich gelegentlich ändern. Wenn das passiert, aktualisieren wir das Datum oben.

Principles.title:
Prinzipien
eines Mythos
Principles.intro: Das sind die von Fjorr. Nicht alles verdient Ausstrahlung.
Principles.p1Body: Ein Protokoll sagt, was geschah. Ein Mythos sagt, was es heißt, lebendig zu sein.
Principles.p2Title: Ein Mythos ist kurz, aber nie seicht.
Principles.p2Body: Ein paar Minuten reichen, jemanden zu verändern — wenn jede Sekunde ihren Platz verdient.
Principles.p3Title: Ein Mythos jagt dem Licht nach.
Principles.p3Body: Das Leben hat Schatten. Wir schauen nicht weg. Wir bleiben auch nicht dort.
Principles.p4Title: Ein Mythos stirbt, wenn er langweilig ist.
Principles.p5Title: Ein Mythos verändert etwas in dir.
Principles.p5Body: Nicht nur gesehen. Gefühlt — und mit hinausgenommen.
Principles.p6Body: Geformt von denen, die ihn tragen, und weitergegeben an die, die noch nicht geboren sind.

Plus.modeInvite: Sign in to mark a moment for the desk.
Plus.bodyPlaceholder: What did you notice? What would you change?
Plus.signInRequired: Sign in to send a note.
Plus.rateLimited: Note limit reached for this film today. Try again tomorrow.
Plus.logsBody: Every note you've left, and where it stands.
Plus.infoP1: Fjorr films aren’t frozen. They can get sharper over time — a cut, a hold, a line, a cue. Walt Disney called it plussing.
Plus.infoP2: In Plus, mark what you notice. If you can make it better yourself — say so. Notes go to the desk, private.
Plus.infoP3: Craft is welcome. The director keeps final say. The archive improves carefully.
Plus.how1: Open any film. Tap Plus in the theater.
Plus.how2: Pause on the moment. Write what you'd change — or what already works.
Plus.how3: Send to the desk. Private. Daily limits apply.
Plus.leadP1: A feature costs too much to risk. A five-minute film doesn't. That's the opening short form has always had — cheap enough to try the wrong idea and find the right one.
Plus.leadP2: Films on Fjorr ship as v1 — not a rough draft, but not the last word either. When something's worth making better, we make it better. We call that the plus.
Plus.whatP1: A film ships when it's ready, not when it's perfect — because perfect doesn't exist on day one. Members can flag what's not landing. If the Cabinet agrees, they plus it: a sharper edit, a better score, a scene that finally works, an idea nobody was brave enough to try the first time. v2 goes live. v1 doesn't disappear — it stays in the changelog, credited, archived, visible.
Plus.whatP2: Nothing gets overwritten. It gets versioned.
Plus.whoP1: Members don't edit films. They file the report. The Cabinet — the director, the editor, the composer, whoever built it — decides if the report's right, and if so, they're the ones who commit the change.
Plus.whoP2: Your name is on your work. It stays your work. v2 is still yours, made by you, because you agreed v1 could be better.
Plus.sectionSubmit: Or you can submit the patch yourself
Plus.submitP1: Sometimes the fix isn't a flag — it's already made. Sometimes it's bolder than a fix: a different score entirely, a cut that takes a real swing. If you can prove it's stronger, submit it. If the Cabinet agrees, it ships, and you're credited on it.
Plus.submitP2: This is how new names get pulled into the Cabinet — not by application, by proof.
Plus.whyP1: A feature can't afford to be wrong. A five-minute film can afford to try. That's not a compromise — it's the one advantage short film has always had over everything else, and almost nobody's used it. Every patch, every resubmission, every wild swing that actually lands is proof the format can hold more risk than anyone's asked of it.
Plus.closing: The best version hasn't shipped yet.
Plus.logsBodyEmpty: Got an idea to make it better? Say so — timestamped to the second. The people who made it decide if you're right. If they agree, they plus it, and a new version ships.
Plus.bureauxRequired: Join the Bureaux to send a note.

Bureaux.headline: Annual membership.
Bureaux.lead: So we're making the opposite bet. Myths raise people. Feeds don't. Short, cinematic films of the world's greatest stories — free, forever, for anyone.
Bureaux.lead2: The Bureaux is how it stays that way. Not a paywall. A choice to fund the thing you believe in, made by the people who show up for it.
